Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

remain verb

be left over

also be left, be left over, what’s left, have left, it remains to

classical

Cato Agr. 2.1: quid restet
Cic. Sen. 46: quī paucī admodum restant
Traupman 370

1restō: short e (Lewis & Short rē-sto). A compound of stō and the prefix re- (de Vaan 516, s.v. re-, red-). Lewis & Short writes rē- before sc, sp and st, and only there. Its article on the prefix gives rĕ, with a by-form rĕd-, and puts the poets’ rēdūcō, rēlātum down to “the suppression of the d”; the long mark before s and a consonant seems to rest on the same idea, as its dī-scindō from dis- does. Bennett (The Latin Language §48) rejects that lengthening for ascendō, distinguō, suspiciō as “an untenable theory of compensatory lengthening”, and Lewis’s own Elementary Latin Dictionary (1890) prints re-spondeō. Ruling: Macrons are spelling.

restō1, restāre, restitī

verb, first conjugation

be left, remain

What is left is the subject, and the person it is left to goes in the dative: nihil mihi restat. “It remains to …” is restat ut with the subjunctive (Traupman 370; Cic. N. D. 2.44, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • supersum, superesse, superfuī — be left over; survive

    verb, irregular (sum) · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3 epil. 1: supersunt mihi quae scrībam; Caes. BG 1.23: bīduum supererat (Lewis & Short)

    Quod superest, as for the rest (Cic. Att. 9.19.3, Lewis & Short).

  • reliquus, reliqua, reliquum — left over, remaining

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.18.4: mūlō istō, quem tibi reliquum dīcis esse

    Reliquum est ut, it remains that; reliquī, the rest, the others.

Examples

  • roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet

    let him ask what work has been done and what is leftCato Agr. 2.1

  • potes mūlō istō, quem tibi reliquum dīcis esse, quoniam canthērium comēdistī, Rōmam pervehī

    you can ride to Rome on that mule you say you have left, since you have eaten your horseCic. Fam. 9.18.4

  • supersunt mihi quae scrībam, sed parcō sciēns

    I have more left to write, but I stop on purposePhaedr. 3 epil. 1

See also leftovers, remain.
